tip.title: Try five minutes of cyclic sighing to settle nerves
tip.why: In a randomized trial of 108 people, five minutes of daily breathing exercises for a month lifted mood and slowed breathing rate, and cyclic sighing (a longer exhale than inhale) showed the largest gains, beating mindfulness meditation. It's a cheap way to settle down before a busy social day.
how: Breathe in through your nose, then add a second short sip of air on top to fill your lungs fully.
Exhale slowly through your mouth for longer than the inhale, as if fogging a mirror.
Repeat for five minutes, once in the morning or before a crowd; stop if you feel dizzy.
tip.ask: I want a five-minute breathing routine to calm down before a big social event. How do I do cyclic sighing, and what does the research say?

markets.headline: The Nasdaq fell 2.6% and chip stocks dropped sharply on AI financing worries, while the Dow finished little changed.
points: Meta fell about 7% even after beating revenue estimates, as investors focused on how much outside funding its AI buildout needs; the cost of insuring its debt rose.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said capital is scarce for the neocloud companies that buy its chips, which revived credit worries. Nvidia fell about 4% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 6.7%, its worst day since June.

Tesla fell 3.1% a day after earnings. Adjusted EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.44 estimate, but net income dropped 42% and Musk trimmed his long-range sales target; lower 2026 capex came with higher spending planned for 2027 and 2028.

Oil rose to a five-month high on Middle East tensions while Treasury yields fell, with the 10-year dipping below 5%. Netflix rose about 3% on its largest buyback ever, and the Dow and Russell 2000 held near flat.

pick.name: Coherent
pick.what: Coherent makes lasers, optical transceivers and materials that move data between AI servers, along with industrial laser systems used in manufacturing and electronics.
pick.why: It sits on the hardware side of AI: the optical links that connect racks of accelerators inside data centers. The stock fell 12.5% on Oct 22 during a sharp drop in optics and chip names, and it is now about 53% below its 52-week high of $440, while analyst consensus still reads Buy with an average target near $410. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: The shares are volatile (beta around 2) and fell roughly 35% in October alone, so the pace of AI data center spending and any guidance change can move the price quickly. Optics stocks tend to fall together when sentiment turns.

btc.summary: In his Oct 22 video, "Bitcoin Bull Market Support Band," and a post the same day, Cowen said a daily close below the 50-day moving average would likely send Bitcoin back to the bull market support band, the zone formed by the 20-week average and 21-week exponential average. The day before he warned that a retest looks likely, and that a second weekly close below the level he calls the line in the sand would make the bullish case hard to defend. He also pointed to a seasonal pattern he calls the "curse of the 21st," which would fit a pre-midterm local top followed by a November low. His own framing is that the Golden Cross still favors bulls, but the Fed leaning toward hikes and weak liquidity are the main reasons for caution.

news.title: Unitree's G1 humanoid output reportedly reaches 10,000 to 20,000 units
news.blurb: Digitimes reports cumulative G1 production at roughly 10,000 to 20,000 units since its May 2024 launch. Unitree itself said in June that G1 output had passed 11,000, so the range is wide and the exact count is not confirmed.
news.ask: What does Unitree's G1 volume mean for pricing and supply-chain costs of humanoid components, and how much of that volume is research and education rather than work deployments?

news.title: South Korea's humanoid effort splits into hands, shipyard bipeds and dual-arm platforms
news.blurb: Digitimes says Tesollo is building dexterous hands, AeiROBOT is preparing its ALICE 5 biped for shipyards and construction sites, and HD Hyundai Robotics is developing a dual-arm platform that could later gain wheels or legs.
news.ask: Is it a sound strategy to build humanoid hands, bipeds and dual-arm bases as separate products, and where do the integration risks sit?

news.title: HD Hyundai Robotics shows a dual-arm robot at FIX 2026
news.blurb: The company's first public showing of the dual-arm robot came at FIX 2026 in Daegu on October 21, as it looks to expand beyond conventional industrial automation.
news.ask: What can a dual-arm fixed or wheeled base do in a factory that a full legged humanoid cannot, and what does it give up?

news.title: Khgears targets humanoid joints, with mass production planned for 2027
news.blurb: The Taiwanese gearmaker is expanding into humanoid robot joint components and expects a newly developed differential reducer to enter mass production in 2027, according to Digitimes.
news.ask: How does a differential reducer differ from the harmonic and planetary reducers common in humanoid joints, and what trade-offs does it offer in backlash, torque density and cost?

news.title: OpenAI reportedly works on a $30B raise at a $1.25T valuation
news.blurb: TechCrunch reports OpenAI is working on a round of up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation ahead of a possible IPO. Terms are still being negotiated and could change.
news.ask: How does a $1.25 trillion valuation square with the AI funding worries behind Thursday's selloff, and what would investors need to believe?

news.title: DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US restrictions
news.blurb: Bloomberg reported the Chinese AI lab raised about $15 billion, days after the US ordered federal civilian agencies to remove its technology, according to TechCrunch.
news.ask: What do the US restrictions on DeepSeek actually cover, and do they affect companies that use its open models?

news.title: Chinese hackers used AI agents after breaching ConnectWise
news.blurb: Microsoft attributes the breach to a China-aligned group that targeted ConnectWise's cloud backup service. TechCrunch reports the attackers reportedly used AI agents against about 2,250 organizations.
news.ask: What should a small engineering team change in its backup and remote-management tooling after a supply-chain breach like ConnectWise?

news.title: Nasdaq falls 2.6% as Meta's spending plans revive AI bubble fears
news.blurb: Meta's higher 2026 capital spending outlook set off a tech selloff on Thursday, with chip stocks hit hard and money moving into defensive sectors.
news.ask: If AI capital gets scarcer, which parts of the robotics supply chain are most exposed, and which are least?

news.title: Tesla plans to expand Cybercab beyond Austin, starting in Dallas
news.blurb: TechCrunch reports the expansion begins in Dallas next month and should reach other cities by the end of the year.
news.ask: What regulatory and operational hurdles decide how fast a driverless fleet can expand city by city, and do they apply to humanoids?

news.title: a16z Crypto rebrands as a16z Frontier, widening to AI and robotics
news.blurb: The practice led by Chris Dixon, which has raised nearly $10B across five funds since 2018, will broaden its focus to AI, robotics and other emerging tech, TechCrunch reports.
news.ask: What does a16z moving a crypto team into robotics suggest about where venture money is heading, and how might it affect humanoid startups' fundraising?

spanish.phrase: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
spanish.pron: nee MOH-doh, yah seh-RAH PAH-rah lah PROHK-see-mah
spanish.meaning: Oh well, there's always next time.
spanish.note: 'Ni modo' is the everyday Mexican shrug for something that can't be changed. Add 'ya será para la próxima' after a missed plan to move on lightly; it's not for serious losses.

dialog.es: Se canceló el partido por la lluvia.
dialog.en: The game was canceled because of the rain.

dialog.es: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima.
dialog.en: Oh well, there's always next time.
Want to go get tacos then?

spanish.use: Say it when a plan falls through and you'd rather move on than complain, like a missed flight or a canceled game.

options: Oh well, there's always next time.

spanish.note: 'No manches' is the everyday Mexican way to say 'no way' or 'you're kidding', and 'padre' means great. Friendly with friends; keep it out of formal settings.

dialog.es: Mira, conseguí boletos para el concierto.
dialog.en: Look, I got tickets for the concert.
And we have spots up front.

spanish.use: Say it next time a friend shares good news, instead of 'wow'.

spanish.note: The everyday Mexican hello between friends. 'Onda' literally means wave, as in vibe. A relaxed reply is 'Nada, aquí nomás.'

dialog.en: What's up! How have you been?

spanish.use: Open your next text to a friend with it instead of 'hey'.

spanish.note: The go-to complaint on a hot day. Add 'hace' for a full sentence: Hace mucho calor.

dialog.en: It's so hot! Want to go get something cold?

dialog.es: Sí, un agua de jamaica bien fría.

spanish.use: Say it the next time you step outside into the afternoon heat, or text it to a friend on a hot day.
